entries.title: Proverbs 19:1
segments: The true worth of a man should be measured by his character, and not by his outward circumstances.  A poor man of truth and wisdom is more honorable in the sight of God, and more useful to his fellow men, than one of great rank and wealth whose life is made up of perverseness and folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:2
segments:
Hasteth with his feet; is rash and inconsiderate in his actions--a common result of the soul's being without knowledge. 
 
Hasty and inconsiderate action comes from the want of true knowledge, and leads to sin.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:3
segments: Men too frequently lay to the account of God's providence the calamities which their own perverseness brings upon them, and thus foolishly fret against the Lord.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:4
segments: The unreasonable deference which is everywhere paid to wealth, is a sad proof of human selfishness and blindness.  The mass of mankind prefer riches without either wisdom or righteousness, to the neglect which attends virtuous poverty.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:10
segments:
Delight; dainty living, which implies ease and affluence. 
 
  Much less for a servant to have rule over princes; that is, a servant retaining a low and servile spirit, which often happens through the favoritism of Eastern monarchs. 
 
When wealth and patronage fall into the hands of the foolish, and the base are exalted above the excellent, the true order of society is perverted, and confusion and misery ensue.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:11
segments:
Deferreth his anger; makes him slow to anger. 
 
Slowness to anger and a forgiving spirit are true marks of a noble soul.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:13
segments: A continual dropping; of water through the roof in a rainy day; which is very common in oriental houses, and very annoying.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:14
segments:
The inheritance of fathers; received from fathers. 
 
  From the Lord; the gift of his providence.  She cannot, like houses and riches, be inherited.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:16
segments: Despiseth his ways; despiseth attention to his ways, because he does not consider himself in danger of going astray.
The man who thinks himself in no danger is near destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:17
segments: The best investment of our property is in deeds of loving-kindness.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:18
segments:
Hope; of his being reclaimed. 
 
  And let not thy soul spare for his crying; the original might be rendered, Desire not to slay him; that is, act not as if it were your desire to destroy him, which you will do if you withhold needed chastisement. 
 
The rod is God's appointment; and the parent who uses it early and discreetly, manifests the truest kindness to his children.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:19
segments: He that is under the control of his angry passions cannot be saved from ruin, either by his own descretion or by the advice and help of his friends.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:21
segments: The subordination of all our plans to the wise counsel of God, constitutes the only sure foundation for peace and tranquillity of spirit.  It is only when we make God's will our will, that we can avoid perpetual disquietude and disappointment.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:22
segments:
The desire of a man is his kindness; a man's kindness is that which makes him an object of affectionate regard, to whom the afflicted and destitute look with longing desire. 
 
  A poor man is better than a liar; that is, a poor man of kindness is better than a rich liar destitute of all goodness. 
 
None but the truly good can gain the true love of their fellow men.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:24
segments: In his bosom; or, in the dish; a figurative way of saying his is too indolent to attend to his own wants.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:25
segments: Scorners are smitten for the good of others; men of understanding are reproved for their own benefit.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:26
segments: No course of conduct brings greater disgrace upon a young men, than to be guilty of squandering his father's estate, and making his mother homeless.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:27
segments: One of the most deadly perils to which the young are exposed, is false doctrine in respect to the principles of religion and morals.  It meets them everywhere, in unprincipled associates, public teachers of error, and corrupt publications.  Without constant vigilance and prayerfulness, they cannot escape its fatal influence.

entries.title: Proverbs 19:28
segments:
Scorneth judgment; has no concern to give his testimony according to truth and equity. 
 
  Devoureth iniquity; feeds upon it as upon a sweet morsel.
